hardFacts.size: India is the 7th largest country in the world and the most populous. It is NOT one destination â€” it is 28 states and 8 union territories, each with distinct language, cuisine, architecture, and culture. Planning India as a single trip is a mistake. Plan by region.
hardFacts.transport: India has the largest railway network in the world (67,000 km). Train travel between major cities is reliable, comfortable in AC classes, and significantly cheaper than flights for journeys under 8 hours. Always book on IRCTC minimum 2 weeks ahead.
hardFacts.currency: Indian Rupee (INR). For foreign visitors: USD 1 = INR 84â€“87. EUR 1 = INR 90â€“95. GBP 1 = INR 108â€“115.
hardFacts.language: 22 official languages. Hindi is spoken across North India. English is widely understood in cities, tourism areas, and by educated population throughout India. South India (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra) uses regional languages more exclusively â€” English is the working language here.
hardFacts.seasons: India has three main seasons: Summer (Marchâ€“June): hot everywhere except the mountains. Monsoon (Juneâ€“September): heavy rain, some areas inaccessible, others extraordinary. Winter (Octoberâ€“February): the correct time for most of India except mountains.
hardFacts.criticalRule: Book train tickets on IRCTC (irctc.co.in) minimum 2 weeks ahead for AC classes. The berths that fill first are 3A (3-tier AC) and 2A (2-tier AC). Never buy train tickets from agents outside the station â€” the IRCTC website or app is the only reliable source. Tourist Quota is available at major stations for foreign visitors.
hardFacts.food: India is the world's best destination for vegetarians. Every region has extraordinary vegetarian cuisine. Even non-vegetarians will eat less meat here than anywhere else and not miss it.
hardFacts.water: NEVER drink tap water anywhere in India. Bottled water from sealed bottles only. Filter or boil when bottled water unavailable. This applies everywhere without exception.

delhi.character: India's capital. 30 million people containing 5,000 years of continuous history. The oldest mosque (Quwwat ul-Islam, 1193 AD), the newest metro, the best street food, and the worst air quality in any major city. Never understood in a single visit.
delhi.bestTime: Octoberâ€“March. Avoid Aprilâ€“June (extreme heat 40â€“45Â°C) and Julyâ€“September (monsoon + heat).
mustDo: Chandni Chowk at 7am â€” before the shops open, wholesale traders working, temples doing morning puja, parathas at Paranthe Wali Gali being fried
Qutub Minar â€” UNESCO, 12th century, finest medieval minaret in Asia, morning before 9am
Humayun's Tomb â€” the prototype for the Taj Mahal, better proportions, a fraction of the tourists
Lodi Garden â€” free, 8am, where Delhi jogs among 15th-century tombs, extraordinary urban park
Karim's restaurant, Jama Masjid area â€” most famous Mughlai restaurant in India, open since 1913
delhi.hiddenGem: Mehrauli Archaeological Park â€” 20+ medieval monuments in a park that most Delhi residents have never visited. Free. Adjacent to Qutub Minar but completely separate and empty.

mustEat: Paranthe Wali Gali, Chandni Chowk â€” stuffed flatbreads with 30 fillings, INR 60â€“150
Karim's near Jama Masjid â€” mutton burra, seekh kebab, INR 200â€“400
Bengali Sweet House, Bengali Market â€” rasgolla, burfi, sandesh, INR 50â€“200
Chhole Bhature at Sita Ram Diwan Chand, Paharganj â€” since 1952, INR 120
Moti Mahal Delux, Daryaganj â€” butter chicken was invented here (claimed)

delhi.policeStation: Delhi Police Control Room: 100. Tourist Police: +91 11 2436 5358
delhi.transport: Delhi Metro: INR 10â€“60 per trip, excellent coverage. Ola/Uber available. Auto-rickshaws: always use meter or prepaid.
delhi.accommodation: Budget: Paharganj area (INR 500â€“1,500). Mid: Connaught Place (INR 3,000â€“8,000). Luxury: The Leela, The Imperial, The Lodhi (INR 15,000â€“50,000).

mumbai.character: India's financial and entertainment capital. More billionaires than Delhi and more slum dwellers than anywhere else simultaneously. The city that accepts everyone and asks nothing in return.
mumbai.bestTime: Novemberâ€“February. Avoid Juneâ€“September (heavy monsoon, though the city itself has extraordinary monsoon energy).
mustDo: Gateway of India at 6am â€” before tour boats and hawkers, the harbour and Taj Mahal Palace Hotel backdrop
Dharavi â€” Asia's most productive slum, guided tour INR 600â€“1,000 through leather, pottery, recycling workshops
Dhobi Ghat â€” world's largest outdoor laundry, view from Mahalaxmi bridge, free
CST (Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus) â€” Victorian Gothic World Heritage station, interior as dramatic as exterior
Juhu Beach at 6pm â€” the city's living room, chaat vendors, cricket, extraordinary cross-section of Mumbai life
mumbai.hiddenGem: Khotachi Wadi â€” a pocket of East Indian Catholic heritage in the middle of the city, wooden bungalows, Christmas stars year-round, no tourists.

mustEat: Vada pav from any street stall â€” the Mumbai breakfast, INR 15â€“25
Britannia & Co, Ballard Estate â€” Parsi Irani cafÃ© since 1923, berry pulao, INR 300â€“500
Bade Miya, Colaba Causeway â€” seekh kebabs under a tree since 1947, INR 200â€“400
Prithvi CafÃ©, Juhu â€” theatre cafÃ©, excellent coffee, INR 100â€“300
Khau Galli night food streets â€” Mohammed Ali Road, Crawford Market area

mumbai.policeStation: Mumbai Police Control Room: 100. Tourist Police: +91 22 2262 0111
mumbai.transport: Local trains: INR 10â€“50, essential and efficient. Metro: limited but growing. Uber/Ola available.
mumbai.accommodation: Budget: Fort/Colaba area (INR 800â€“2,000). Mid: Bandra (INR 4,000â€“10,000). Luxury: Taj Mahal Palace, Four Seasons (INR 20,000â€“80,000).
mumbai.budgetPerDay: INR 2,000â€“4,000 (Mumbai is India's most expensive city)

kolkata.character: India's cultural capital. The city of Tagore, Subhas Chandra Bose, and Mother Teresa. Intellectual, artistic, politically passionate. The finest street food in India. Decaying colonial grandeur that is currently being re-evaluated.
kolkata.bestTime: Octoberâ€“March. Durga Puja (October) is the most extraordinary festival in India.
mustDo: Victoria Memorial at dawn â€” the finest colonial building in Asia, free gardens
Howrah Bridge at 5am â€” 100,000 vehicles and pedestrians cross daily, the engineering is extraordinary
College Street book market â€” the largest second-hand book market in the world
Kumartuli â€” the neighbourhood where the clay idols for Durga Puja are made year-round
Evening at a adda (tea stall intellectual gathering) in North Kolkata
kolkata.hiddenGem: Tiretti Bazaar, Chinatown â€” the oldest Chinatown in India, the Chinese morning dim sum breakfast at 5am.

mustEat: Kathi rolls from Nizam's, New Market â€” invented here in 1932, INR 80â€“150
Mishti doi and rosogolla from any sweet shop â€” the Bengali originals, INR 20â€“60
Mutton biryani from Arsalan, Park Circus â€” the best biryani in India (contested), INR 250â€“400
Phuchka (Kolkata's pani puri) â€” different from North Indian version, must compare, INR 30â€“60
Fish curry and rice from any Bengali dhaba â€” the city's soul food

kolkata.transport: Metro: INR 5â€“25. Yellow taxis (metered). Trams (historic, still operating). Rickshaws in some areas.

bangalore.character: India's Silicon Valley. A garden city transformed by IT money. The best microbrewery culture in India. A comfortable, cosmopolitan base for South India exploration.
bangalore.bestTime: Year-round (1,000m elevation keeps it pleasant). Peak summer 28â€“33Â°C.
mustDo: Cubbon Park morning walk â€” 300 acres in the city centre, birdwatching, free
Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace â€” 18th-century wooden palace, INR 15
Bangalore Palace â€” the Wadiyar royal palace in Gothic-Tudor style, INR 230
Commercial Street for shopping â€” the real Bangalore shopping strip
IISc campus â€” India's finest research institution, free to walk the grounds

mustEat: Masala dosa at MTR (Mavalli Tiffin Rooms) â€” since 1924, INR 120â€“200
Benne dosa (butter dosa) at Vidyarthi Bhavan â€” since 1943, INR 60â€“100
Craft beer at Arbor or Toit brewery â€” Bangalore's microbrewery culture, INR 300â€“500
Coorgi pork curry at any Coorg restaurant â€” specific to this region

hyderabad.character: The city of the Nizams, biryani, and new technology. The old city (Charminar area) and the new city (Hi-Tech City) are literally different countries 15km apart.
mustDo: Charminar at sunset â€” the 1591 monument, the evening market around it is extraordinary
Golconda Fort â€” the Qutb Shahi dynasty fortress, acoustic demonstration (a clap at the main gate heard 1km away)
Salar Jung Museum â€” one of the largest single-person art collections in the world, INR 50
Hyderabadi dum biryani cooking class â€” learn the original recipe
hyderabad.hiddenGem: Paigah Tombs â€” the mausoleum of the Paigah nobles, extraordinary Mughal architecture, almost no tourists, free.

mustEat: Paradise Biryani â€” the most famous biryani restaurant in India, INR 250â€“400
Haleem at Shah Ghouse near Charminar â€” the definitive Hyderabadi haleem, INR 150â€“250
Double ka meetha (bread pudding) â€” specific to Hyderabad, INR 80â€“120
Irani chai at any Irani cafÃ© near Charminar â€” the specific Hyderabadi tea culture

chennai.character: India's gateway to South India. The most culturally Tamil city. Classical music and dance (Carnatic music season December). The Marina Beach (second longest in the world). The Kapaleeshwarar Temple.
chennai.bestTime: Novemberâ€“February. Avoid Mayâ€“June (extreme humidity and heat).
mustDo: Kapaleeshwarar Temple, Mylapore â€” active 7th-century Dravidian temple, free
Marina Beach at 6am â€” 13km beach, the morning is extraordinary (hawkers, children, fishermen)
Fort St. George â€” the first English fortress in India (1644), museum, INR 5
Mahabalipuram day trip â€” UNESCO rock-cut temples, 60km south

mustEat: Filter coffee and idli-sambar from any Saravana Bhavan â€” the South Indian standard
Chettinad chicken curry â€” the most complex South Indian cuisine, any Chettinad restaurant
Fish curry rice â€” the Tamil Nadu daily meal
Murukku and sundal from street vendors on Marina Beach

rajasthan.overview: The most visually extraordinary state in India. Every city is a different colour â€” Blue City (Jodhpur), Pink City (Jaipur), White City (Udaipur), Golden City (Jaisalmer). The palaces were built by kings who competed for aesthetic supremacy.
rajasthan.bestTime: Octoberâ€“March. Avoid Aprilâ€“June (extreme heat 40â€“45Â°C). Julyâ€“September: monsoon brings green but some roads flood.

jaipur.character: The Pink City. The most organised tourist infrastructure in Rajasthan. Gateway to the Golden Triangle.
mustDo: Amber Fort (Amer Fort) â€” arrive 8am before tour groups. The finest Mughal-Rajput fort in India. INR 500 foreigners.
Hawa Mahal exterior at golden hour â€” best photograph at 5:30pm from the street across
Johri Bazaar â€” the silver jewellery market, best Rajasthani silver in India
City Palace â€” still occupied by the Jaipur royal family, INR 700
jaipur.food: Dal baati churma (INR 200â€“350), Ghewar sweet (INR 100â€“200), Kulfi at Rawat Mishtan Bhandar
jaipur.hiddenGem: Panna Meena ka Kund â€” an extraordinary 16th-century stepwell in Amer town, almost no tourists, free.
jaipur.accommodation: Budget: INR 800â€“2,000. Heritage haveli hotels: INR 3,000â€“10,000. Luxury: Rambagh Palace (INR 30,000+).

jodhpur.character: The Blue City. The most dramatic fort in India. The most atmospheric old city in Rajasthan.
mustDo: Mehrangarh Fort â€” the finest fort in Rajasthan. On a hill 122m above the city. INR 600 foreigners.
Blue city rooftop at sunrise â€” from the fort battlements, the blue houses below
Ghantaghar (Clock Tower) market â€” the most vibrant local market in Jodhpur
jodhpur.food: Makhaniya lassi (saffron lassi), Mawa kachori (sweet-stuffed fried bread), Mirchi vada (chilli fritters). Best at On the Rocks restaurant or any haveli cafÃ©.
jodhpur.hiddenGem: The old city lanes below Mehrangarh at night â€” navigated by the sound of the fort above, every turn reveals a different angle of the same wall. Free.
jodhpur.accommodation: Budget: INR 700â€“1,500. Heritage: Raas Haveli, RAAS (INR 8,000â€“20,000).

udaipur.character: The White City. The Lake City. The most romantic city in India. The lakes, the City Palace, the boat rides.
mustDo: City Palace â€” the largest palace complex in Rajasthan, INR 300. The museum and the rooftop views are extraordinary.
Boat ride at sunset on Lake Pichola â€” the Lake Palace visible, INR 400â€“700
Jagdish Temple â€” active 17th-century Vishnu temple in the middle of the city, free
Bagore Ki Haveli cultural show â€” traditional Rajasthani folk performance, INR 150
udaipur.food: Daal baati churma, Laal maas (red mutton curry), Mawa kachori. Best restaurants on the rooftops overlooking Lake Pichola.
udaipur.hiddenGem: Eklingji Temple 22km north â€” the Maharana's personal temple, open for morning puja at 4am, most spiritually atmospheric place in Rajasthan. Almost no tourists.
udaipur.accommodation: Budget: INR 800â€“2,000. Lake view heritage: INR 4,000â€“15,000. The Oberoi Udaivilas: INR 40,000+.

jaisalmer.character: The Golden City. A living fort city in the Thar Desert. The most extraordinary overnight experience in India â€” desert camping.
mustDo: Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Quila) â€” a UNESCO living fort, still inhabited. The best-preserved medieval fort in Asia.
Patwon ki Haveli â€” the most elaborate carved merchant mansion in Rajasthan, INR 100
Sam sand dunes sunrise â€” arrive before any other tourist at 5am. INR 0 to access the dunes.
Desert overnight camping â€” at least one night in the dunes, watching the stars with no light pollution
jaisalmer.food: Ker sangri (desert bean and berry curry), Bajre ki roti (millet bread), Mutton biryani at the fort base restaurants.
jaisalmer.hiddenGem: Kuldhara abandoned village â€” a whole Paliwal Brahmin village abandoned overnight in 1825, preserved as it was, ghost town feel, INR 50.
jaisalmer.accommodation: In-fort guesthouses: INR 600â€“1,500. Desert camps: INR 1,500â€“5,000 (basic to luxury tents).

kerala.overview: India's most literate state. The backwaters, the Malabar cuisine, Kathakali, spice country, tea estates. The least aggressive tourist culture in India. The best food in India by most serious measures.
kerala.bestTime: Octoberâ€“May. Juneâ€“September: monsoon â€” beautiful but most houseboat services limited.

kochi.character: Fort Kochi is India's most photogenic colonial quarter â€” Portuguese, Dutch, and British layers in one street. Chinese fishing nets at sunrise. The Jew Town spice market.
mustDo: Chinese fishing nets (cheena vala) at sunrise â€” the symbol of Kerala, best before 7am when fishermen are working
Mattancherry Palace (Dutch Palace) â€” 16th century, extraordinary Kerala murals, INR 5
Jew Town and Paradesi Synagogue â€” the 450-year-old synagogue, the spice warehouse district, INR 5
Kathakali performance â€” traditional dance-drama, evening shows at Kerala Kathakali Centre, INR 300â€“500
kochi.food: Kerala fish curry (the coconut-based version), Appam with stew, Parotta and beef curry, Puttu and kadala curry. Best at Dhe Puttu or any local toddy shop.
kochi.hiddenGem: Kumbalangi Integrated Tourism Village â€” a genuine working fishing village 12km from Kochi, traditional coir and fish curing, free to walk.
kochi.accommodation: Fort Kochi heritage guesthouses: INR 1,500â€“6,000. Malabar House: INR 8,000+.

alleppey_backwaters.character: The Venice of the East. 1,500km of canals, lakes, rivers, and lagoons. Houseboat stays are the correct way to experience this.
mustDo: Houseboat overnight stay â€” at least 24 hours on the backwaters. INR 8,000â€“15,000 for 2-person boat.
Nehru Trophy Boat Race (second Saturday August) â€” the largest snake boat race in India
Village tour by country boat â€” smaller, quieter canals inaccessible to houseboats, INR 300â€“500
Sunrise on the backwaters â€” the best hour of the backwater experience
alleppey_backwaters.food: Karimeen pollichathu (pearl spot fish in banana leaf) â€” the signature backwater dish, INR 350â€“500. Prawn moilee (coconut curry).
alleppey_backwaters.hiddenGem: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary â€” the best birdwatching in Kerala, dawn canoe tours, INR 300.
alleppey_backwaters.accommodation: Budget: Alleppey town guesthouses INR 800â€“2,000. Houseboat INR 8,000â€“15,000/night.

munnar.character: The finest tea estate landscape in India at 1,600m elevation. Misty mornings. The Eravikulam National Park with Nilgiri tahr.
mustDo: Tea estate walk at dawn â€” the KDHP tea estates allow walking. The mist in the tea gardens at 6am.
Eravikulam National Park â€” home to the Nilgiri tahr (mountain goat), INR 200 foreigners
Top Station viewpoint â€” the highest point in Munnar with views into Tamil Nadu
Tea Museum, Nallathanni Estate â€” how tea is made, INR 75
munnar.food: Kerala sadya (banana leaf feast of 25 dishes), parotta and beef, toddy from a local shop.
munnar.accommodation: Tea estate stays: INR 3,000â€“10,000. Budget guesthouses in town: INR 800â€“2,000.

varkala.character: A beach town on red laterite cliffs. The alternative to Kovalam. Better food, fewer crowds, the natural spring on the beach.
mustDo: North Cliff at sunset â€” the cliffside walk with the beach 30 metres below
Janardhana Swami Temple â€” 2,000-year-old Vishnu temple on the cliff edge, free
varkala.food: Seafood at cliff restaurants â€” tiger prawns, fish curry, coconut rice.

rajasthan_golden_triangle.overview: Delhiâ€“Agraâ€“Jaipur is India's most visited circuit. Can be done in 5â€“7 days by train.

agra.character: The city of the Taj Mahal. Agra itself is chaotic and polluted but the monuments justify everything.
mustDo: Taj Mahal at sunrise â€” CRITICAL. Arrive at gate opening 30 minutes before sunrise. The most photographed building in human history looks different at 6am from 2pm. INR 1,100 foreigners.
Agra Fort â€” Akbar's red sandstone fort, 2km from Taj. The view of the Taj from Musamman Burj where Shah Jahan died captive. INR 650 foreigners.
Mehtab Bagh garden â€” directly across the river from the Taj, sunset view of the Taj from the opposite bank, almost no tourists, INR 300.
agra.food: Petha sweet (translucent pumpkin candy specific to Agra), dal moth, biryani at Pinch of Spice restaurant.
agra.hiddenGem: Itmad-ud-Daulah tomb (Baby Taj) â€” the Taj Mahal's prototype, marble inlay as fine as the Taj, almost no visitors, INR 310 foreigners.
agra.accommodation: Budget: INR 800â€“2,500. Luxury: The Oberoi Amarvilas (Taj view from every room, INR 35,000+).

ladakh.overview: The highest accessible plateau in India. Buddhist monasteries 1,000 years old. Mountains above 6,000m. The Indus River. The clearest sky in Asia. A different country inside India.
ladakh.bestTime: Juneâ€“September. Passes open late May. October: first snow on passes. Novemberâ€“May: many passes closed, limited activities.
ladakh.acclimatisation: CRITICAL. Leh is at 3,524m. Arrive by flight (not road) and rest for 48 hours before any activity. Altitude sickness is real and dangerous â€” headache, nausea, shortness of breath. Ascend slowly.
mustDo: Pangong Lake â€” 4,225m, the blue-green lake extending into China, 5 hours from Leh, camping on the shore
Diskit Monastery, Nubra Valley â€” ancient monastery with enormous Maitreya Buddha statue
Khardung La pass â€” 5,359m (one of the world's highest motorable roads), accessible by shared taxi from Leh
Lamayuru Monastery â€” oldest monastery in Ladakh, stark moonscape landscape, genuine living monastery
The Zanskar River trek â€” one of the finest multi-day treks in India
ladakh.food: Thukpa (noodle soup), Momos, Tsampa (roasted barley), Butter tea (acquired taste). Tibetan and Ladakhi cuisine.
ladakh.hiddenGem: Turtuk village â€” near the Pakistan border, only opened to tourists in 2010. The northernmost village accessible in India. Balti culture and apricot orchards.
ladakh.accommodation: Budget homestays: INR 800â€“1,500 (includes dinner and breakfast). Mid guesthouses: INR 2,000â€“5,000. Hotel Grand Dragon (luxury): INR 8,000+.
ladakh.transport: Shared taxis between Leh and major sites: INR 300â€“800/person. Private taxis: INR 3,000â€“8,000/day. Own vehicle essential for Nubra and Pangong.
ladakh.permits: Inner Line Permit required for Pangong, Nubra, and border areas. Available online (ladakhadventure.com) or at Leh DC office. INR 200â€“400 per area.

himachal_pradesh.overview: The Himalayan state. Shimla, Manali, Dharamshala, and the extraordinary Spiti Valley. The mountains accessible from Delhi.

shimla.character: The former summer capital of British India. A hill station at 2,205m with Victorian architecture, the Ridge, Christ Church, and the Jakhu Temple.
shimla.bestTime: Aprilâ€“June (pleasant hill station summer). Octoberâ€“November (apple harvest). Decemberâ€“January (snow, if that's the goal).
mustDo: The Ridge evening walk â€” the central spine of Shimla, Christ Church, the Mall
Jakhu Temple â€” 2.5km walk or shared taxi, monkey-infested Hanuman temple above the city, extraordinary views
Toy Train (Kalka-Shimla Railway) â€” UNESCO World Heritage narrow-gauge railway, 5 hours from Kalka, INR 50â€“400
shimla.food: Himachali dham (traditional feast), Siddu (steamed bread with walnut paste), Trout fish from Beas River.
shimla.accommodation: Budget: Mall Road guesthouses INR 800â€“2,000. Wildflower Hall: INR 18,000+ (finest mountain hotel).

manali.character: The adventure capital of North India. 2,050m altitude. Gateway to Rohtang Pass, Spiti, and the Leh-Manali Highway.
mustDo: Rohtang Pass (3,978m) â€” snow year-round, extraordinary mountain scenery, INR 500 permit + taxi
Old Manali village â€” the genuine village above tourist Manali, apple orchards, Hadimba Temple
Hadimba Devi Temple â€” a 1553 wooden temple in a deodar cedar forest, free
River rafting on the Beas â€” Grade 2â€“4 rapids, INR 600â€“1,200
manali.food: Sidu, trout, Himachali dham, Tibetan momos at Old Manali cafÃ©s.
manali.hiddenGem: Naggar Castle â€” a 16th-century castle 22km from Manali, breathtaking views, almost no tourists, INR 50.

dharamshala_mcleod_ganj.character: The seat of the Tibetan government-in-exile. The Dalai Lama's residence. Tibetan Buddhism, monasteries, and the best momos in India.
mustDo: Tsuglagkhang Temple Complex â€” the Dalai Lama's residence, main temple, museum, free
Dharamkot village walk â€” the village above McLeod Ganj, Israeli-influenced cafÃ©s, mountain views
Norbulingka Institute â€” Tibetan arts and crafts preservation, extraordinary architecture, INR 50
dharamshala_mcleod_ganj.food: Tibetan momos (the best in India), Thukpa, butter tea, bakeries in McLeod Ganj.

spiti_valley.character: The most dramatic mountain valley accessible by road in India. At 3,800â€“4,500m. Monasteries, the Spiti River, moonscapes.
spiti_valley.bestTime: Juneâ€“September only. Completely closed in winter.
mustDo: Key Monastery (Ki Gompa) â€” the most dramatically sited monastery in India, above the Spiti River
Kibber village â€” one of the highest villages in the world accessible by road (4,200m)
Dhankar Lake â€” 4,200m trek above Dhankar village, extraordinary views
spiti_valley.hiddenGem: Pin Valley National Park â€” snow leopard territory, the best chance of snow leopard sighting in India with a local guide.
spiti_valley.accommodation: Homestays in villages: INR 800â€“1,500 including meals. No luxury options.

uttarakhand.overview: Devbhoomi â€” the Land of the Gods. Rishikesh, Haridwar, the Char Dham pilgrimage, Jim Corbett, the Nanda Devi massif.

rishikesh.character: The Yoga Capital of the World. Where the Beatles came in 1968. The Ganga emerging from the Himalayas. The adventure sports capital of North India.
rishikesh.bestTime: Octoberâ€“April. Avoid Juneâ€“August (monsoon â€” river too high for rafting).
mustDo: Laxman Jhula suspension bridge at dawn â€” the Ganga in morning light, temples on both banks
Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat â€” evening ceremony, free, extraordinary atmosphere
River rafting on the Ganga â€” Grade 2â€“4 rapids, INR 800â€“1,500
Yoga class at one of the ashrams â€” Parmarth Niketan or Sivananda Ashram
rishikesh.food: The vegetarian food in Rishikesh is extraordinary â€” the Israeli, Tibetan, and South Indian restaurants along the ghats. Chole bhature, banana pancakes, thali.
rishikesh.hiddenGem: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple â€” 34km above Rishikesh, the most sacred Shiva temple in the region, set against the Garhwal Himalayas, almost no foreign tourists.
rishikesh.accommodation: Budget: INR 400â€“1,200 (ashram stays from INR 200). Mid: INR 2,000â€“5,000. Luxury: Ananda in the Himalayas (INR 30,000+).

haridwar.character: One of the four sacred cities of Hindu pilgrimage. The Ganga after descending from the Himalayas. The Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri is the most famous religious evening in India.
mustDo: Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri ghat â€” every evening at sunset, the most photographed religious ceremony in India
Har Ki Pauri ghat at 5am â€” when devotees take their sacred bath before sunrise

nainital.character: A lake town in the Kumaon hills. Colonial-era buildings, boat rides, the Mall Road.
mustDo: Nainital Lake boat ride
Naini Devi Temple
Snow View Point via cable car (INR 175)
nainital.accommodation: Budget: INR 800â€“2,000. The Naini Retreat: INR 5,000+.

northeast_india.overview: India's most overlooked region. Eight states with distinct languages, cuisines, and cultures. Meghalaya, Assam, Nagaland, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura. Requires Inner Line Permit for most states.

meghalaya.character: The wettest place on earth. Living root bridges (grown from rubber tree roots over 500 years). Cherrapunji and Mawsynram. The cleanest rivers in Asia.
mustDo: Double Decker Living Root Bridge, Nongriat village â€” 3,000-step descent into rainforest. The most extraordinary natural structure in India. Free.
Nohkalikai Falls â€” the tallest plunge waterfall in India (340m), near Cherrapunji
Dawki river and its transparent water â€” the most transparent natural water in India
meghalaya.permits: No ILP required for Indian citizens. Foreign nationals: Restricted Area Permit for some areas.
meghalaya.bestTime: Octoberâ€“May. Juneâ€“September: extreme monsoon (Mawsynram receives the most rainfall on earth).

assam.character: Tea country. One-horned rhinoceros. The Brahmaputra River. Kaziranga National Park.
mustDo: Kaziranga National Park â€” highest density of one-horned rhinoceroses in the world. Jeep safari INR 3,500. UNESCO World Heritage.
Majuli Island â€” largest river island in the world, neo-Vaishnavite culture, accessible by ferry
Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati â€” one of the most important Shakti temples in India
assam.food: Assamese thali, tenga (sour fish curry), pitha (rice cakes), Assam tea from source.

sikkim.character: India's smallest state and first organic state. Buddhist monasteries, the Himalayas, rhododendron forests. Kanchenjunga (world's third highest mountain) visible from Gangtok.
mustDo: Rumtek Monastery â€” the most important Karma Kagyu monastery outside Tibet
Nathula Pass (4,310m) â€” the India-China border pass, accessible from Gangtok with permit
Yumthang Valley â€” the Valley of Flowers, 3,564m, INR 200 permit
sikkim.permits: ILP required for Indian citizens. Protected Area Permit for foreign nationals.

andaman_islands.overview: The finest islands in India. The Andaman Sea. Havelock (Radhanagar Beach â€” Asia's best beach), Neil Island (more secluded), Port Blair (the capital).
andaman_islands.permits: Indian citizens: no permit needed. Foreign nationals: Restricted Area Permit (issued on arrival at Port Blair airport).
mustDo: Radhanagar Beach, Havelock â€” consistently ranked Asia's best beach
Elephant Beach snorkelling â€” coral reefs, sea turtles, INR 500 boat
Cellular Jail, Port Blair â€” the British colonial prison where freedom fighters were held, INR 30
Scuba diving â€” one of the best diving in India, visibility 25â€“30m, Indian Ocean marine life
andaman_islands.food: Seafood: grilled tuna, lobster, prawn curry. The fish here was caught that morning.
andaman_islands.transport: Port Blair to Havelock: government ferry INR 420 or speedboat INR 1,000â€“1,500 each way.
andaman_islands.accommodation: Havelock: Beach No. 5 guesthouses INR 1,500â€“4,000. Eco resort on Radhanagar: INR 5,000â€“15,000.
andaman_islands.bestTime_detail: Februaryâ€“April for best diving visibility. Novemberâ€“January: pleasant weather and relatively uncrowded.

varanasi.overview: The oldest continuously inhabited city in the world. The spiritual capital of Hinduism. Witnessing life and death simultaneously on the same ghats. Not for everyone.
varanasi.bestTime: Octoberâ€“March. Avoid Aprilâ€“June (extreme heat). Dev Diwali (November) is extraordinary.
mustDo: Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat â€” every evening at sunset, 20+ priests performing fire ceremony in synchrony
Morning boat ride at 5am â€” before sunrise, the ghats being used for yoga, bathing, laundry, prayer, cremation simultaneously
Manikarnika Ghat â€” the cremation ghat burning 24 hours. Witnessing respectfully from distance.
Narrow lanes of the old city â€” getting lost is mandatory. Every turn reveals a temple, a sweet shop, a silk weaver.
Sarnath â€” 10km from Varanasi, where the Buddha gave his first sermon, INR 200
varanasi.food: Kachori sabzi (INR 30), Malaiyo (winter morning sweet, INR 50), Banarasi paan, Lassi at Blue Lassi shop.
varanasi.hiddenGem: Tulsi Ghat at 5am â€” quieter than Dashashwamedh, a fishing community also lives here. The combination of fishing boats, temple bells, and river is the most genuine Varanasi experience.
varanasi.important: Touts at Varanasi are aggressive â€” boat touts especially. Fix price before boarding any boat. Authorised rate: INR 200â€“400/hour for the full boat.
varanasi.accommodation: Heritage ghats guesthouses: INR 800â€“3,000. Luxury: Brijrama Palace (on the Ganga, INR 15,000+).

karnataka.overview: Bangalore, Mysore, Hampi, Coorg, and the extraordinary Hoysala temples.

mysore.character: India's cleanest city. Mysore Palace (most visited monument after the Taj), silk, sandalwood, Dussehra festival.
mustDo: Mysore Palace â€” the maharaja's palace lit with 100,000 lights on Sunday evenings and during Dussehra, INR 200 foreigners
Chamundi Hill â€” the hill above Mysore with Chamundeshwari Temple, city view
Devaraja Market â€” 19th-century covered market, largest flower market in South India
Silk weaving factory â€” Karnataka Silk Industries Corporation, see silk made
mysore.food: Mysore pak (the original), Mysore masala dosa, set dosa.
mysore.hiddenGem: Somnathpur Hoysala Temple â€” 13km from Mysore, the most perfectly preserved Hoysala temple, extraordinary star-shaped sculpture, almost no tourists, INR 25.
mysore.bestTime: Octoberâ€“March. Dussehra festival (October) â€” the most spectacular public festival in South India.

hampi.character: UNESCO World Heritage ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire across a boulder landscape unlike anywhere else on earth. The ruins of a city that was once the second largest in the world.
mustDo: Virupaksha Temple â€” still active, 7th century, the sunrise view from the gopuram (INR 0 to enter)
Vittala Temple â€” the famous stone chariot and musical pillars, INR 600 foreigners
Matanga Hill sunrise â€” 30-minute climb, 360Â° view of ruins, boulders, and paddy fields
Hippie Island (Virupapur Gaddi) across the river â€” the bohemian community across the Tungabhadra
hampi.food: Unlimited thali restaurants (INR 100â€“150), banana pancakes, filter coffee.
hampi.hiddenGem: Anegundi â€” the village across the river, the ancient capital before Hampi, almost no tourists, traditional pottery and crafts.
hampi.accommodation: Guesthouses in Hampi Bazaar: INR 400â€“1,500. Across the river: INR 600â€“2,000.

coorg.character: India's Scotland. Coffee and cardamom estates in the Western Ghats. Misty hills, waterfalls, home-stays in plantation houses.
mustDo: Coffee plantation walk â€” walk through an estate picking and learning coffee processing
Abbey Falls â€” in the middle of coffee and spice plantations, free
Raja's Seat, Madikeri â€” the sunset viewpoint of Coorg
Dubare Elephant Camp â€” elephant bathing in the Cauvery River, INR 150
coorg.food: Coorg pork curry (unique to this community), Pandi curry, Kadambuttu (rice dumplings), Akki roti.
coorg.accommodation: Plantation homestays: INR 3,000â€“8,000 including meals. Orange County Resort: INR 12,000+.

tamil_nadu.overview: The heartland of Dravidian culture. The most extraordinary temple architecture in India. Excellent food. The Chettinad cuisine region.

madurai.character: The temple city. The Meenakshi Amman Temple is the most extraordinary active temple in India.
mustDo: Meenakshi Amman Temple â€” active temple complex with 14 gopurams, the most impressive Hindu temple architecture in existence. Free entry (INR 50 for camera). Go at 5am when the morning puja begins.
Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace â€” the 17th-century Nayaka ruler's palace, INR 50
madurai.food: Jigarthanda (local cold drink unique to Madurai), Kari dosa, Chettinad cuisine (30km away in Karaikudi).
madurai.hiddenGem: Gandhi Memorial Museum, Madurai â€” the museum where Gandhi's blood-stained dhoti is preserved from his assassination. Free. Deeply moving.

mahabalipuram.character: UNESCO World Heritage coastal temple town. Shore Temple, the Five Rathas (rock-cut chariots), the enormous bas-relief of Arjuna's Penance.
mustDo: Shore Temple at sunrise â€” 7th-8th century, on the Bay of Bengal, INR 600 foreigners
Arjuna's Penance â€” the world's largest bas-relief, 9x27m, carved in the 7th century, free
Five Rathas â€” monolithic rock-cut temples, INR 600

gujarat.overview: The land of Gandhi, the Rann of Kutch, the last Asiatic lions, and the most extraordinary salt desert in the world.

ahmedabad.character: India's first UNESCO World Heritage city. The walled city has 600 years of continuous habitation, extraordinary pol neighbourhoods, and excellent food.
mustDo: Old City pol walk â€” the traditional neighbourhood system of Ahmedabad, the finest surviving urban heritage in Gujarat
Sabarmati Ashram â€” Mahatma Gandhi's home, from which the Dandi Salt March began, free
Adalaj Vav stepwell â€” one of the finest carved stepwells in India, free
Swaminarayan Akshardham â€” the BAPS temple (one of 3 in the world), free
ahmedabad.food: Dhokla, khandvi, fafda-jalebi, Gujarati thali (unlimited). Best at Agashiye (rooftop restaurant in heritage haveli), Gordhan Thal for thali.
ahmedabad.hiddenGem: Modhera Sun Temple â€” the finest sun temple in India, 102km from Ahmedabad, almost no tourists, INR 100.

rann_of_kutch.character: The largest salt desert in the world. The Great Rann stretches 7,500 sq km. The white salt flats at sunset and sunrise are among the most extraordinary landscapes on earth.
mustDo: Rann Utsav â€” the cultural festival Novemberâ€“February, with the white salt flats under a full moon
Kalo Dungar (Black Hill) â€” the highest point in Kutch, views of the Rann
Bhuj Aina Mahal â€” the palace of mirrors
rann_of_kutch.accommodation: Rann Utsav tent city: INR 5,000â€“15,000 including meals.

punjab.overview: The heartland of Sikh culture. Amritsar and the Golden Temple. The land of mustard fields in winter.

amritsar.character: The holiest city for Sikhs. The Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) is the most spiritually overwhelming and most generous place in India â€” the langar (community kitchen) feeds 100,000 people daily for free.
mustDo: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) â€” open 24 hours, free entry, free langar (community meal). The most peaceful hour: 4am when the first prayers begin.
Langar â€” eat the free community meal alongside Sikhs, pilgrims, and travellers. The largest free kitchen in the world.
Wagah Border ceremony â€” 30km from Amritsar, the daily flag-lowering ceremony at the India-Pakistan border, free
Jallianwala Bagh â€” the memorial garden where the British Massacre of 1919 occurred, free
amritsar.food: Amritsari kulcha (stuffed bread with chickpeas), lassi at Gurdas Ram, fish tikka at famous restaurants on Lawrence Road.
amritsar.hiddenGem: Akal Takht inside the Golden Temple complex â€” the highest Sikh temporal seat, more architecturally extraordinary than the Golden Temple itself and completely overlooked by most visitors.
amritsar.accommodation: Budget: near Golden Temple INR 600â€“1,500. Heritage: Mrs. Bhandari's Guesthouse (colonial home, INR 3,000+).
amritsar.transport: Amritsar has good rail connections from Delhi (5â€“6 hours). From Chandigarh (3 hours). The city is small â€” walk or auto-rickshaw everywhere.

odisha.overview: The most undervisited major state in India. Puri, Konark Sun Temple, Chilika Lake (Asia's largest brackish water lagoon), and the Jagannath Temple.
mustDo: Konark Sun Temple â€” the 13th-century UNESCO temple in the shape of a massive chariot, INR 600 foreigners
Puri Jagannath Temple â€” one of the four sacred dhams of Hinduism (non-Hindus cannot enter the inner sanctum)
Chilika Lake â€” the pink flamingos, Irrawaddy dolphins, migratory birds
odisha.hiddenGem: Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves â€” 2,000-year-old Jain caves carved into rock, almost no tourists, INR 25 foreigners.

budgetTravelIndia.philosophy: India is the world's finest destination for intelligent budget travel. The secret: eat where locals eat, use public transport, stay in locally-owned guesthouses rather than hotel chains.

trainTravel.whyTrain: The Indian Railways network connects 7,000+ stations. For journeys under 8 hours, trains are faster than flights when airport time is factored in, and dramatically cheaper.

classes.sleeper_SL: INR 200â€“400 for most long journeys. Basic but functional. AC compartments exist for the privileged few.
classes.3A: 3-tier AC, INR 500â€“1,200. The best value for comfort. Curtain privacy.

trainTravel.booking: IRCTC.co.in is the official site. Download the IRCTC Rail Connect app. Tourist Quota (5â€“10 seats per train reserved for foreign tourists, available at major station PRS counters). Tatkal quota: emergency booking 1 day before at 30% premium.

bestRoutes.delhi_jaipur: 4.5 hours, 14 trains daily. Shatabdi Express best.
bestRoutes.mumbai_goa: 8â€“12 hours, Konkan Railway is the most scenic railway in India.
bestRoutes.kolkata_darjeeling: NJP to Darjeeling by Toy Train (UNESCO) â€” 8 hours on the narrow-gauge

food.strategy: Eat at dhabas (roadside restaurants) for most meals. Order thali whenever available. Never eat at restaurants attached to tourist sites.

budgetPerMeal.street_breakfast: INR 20â€“60 (poha, idli, paratha, vada pav by region)
budgetPerMeal.temple_langar: Free â€” Sikh gurdwaras, Krishna temples
budgetPerMeal.tourist_restaurant: INR 300â€“600 for inferior version of same food

food.freeFood: Sikh Gurudwaras serve free langar (community meal) to anyone regardless of religion, nationality, or wealth. The langar at Golden Temple Amritsar feeds 100,000 people daily. Always accept if offered.

regionalGuide.south: Masala dosa, idli-sambar, Kerala fish curry, Chettinad chicken, Hyderabadi biryani
regionalGuide.west: Pav bhaji (Mumbai), vada pav (Maharashtra), dhokla (Gujarat), Rajasthani dal baati churma, Goan fish curry
regionalGuide.east: Macher jhol (Bengali fish curry), rosogolla (Bengali sweet origin), momos (Northeast)

indianFestivals.diwali: Octoberâ€“November. The Festival of Lights. Most spectacular in Varanasi (River of Lights on the Ganga), Jaipur, and Amritsar. Book accommodation 2â€“3 months ahead for Varanasi Diwali.
indianFestivals.holi: March. The Festival of Colours. Most intense in Mathura-Vrindavan (INR 300â€“1,000 for organised events) and Rajasthan. Wear clothes you can discard.
indianFestivals.dussehra: October. Victory of good over evil. Mysore celebrates most grandly â€” the Mysore Palace illuminated with 100,000 lights for 10 nights.
indianFestivals.navratri_garba: Septemberâ€“October. Nine nights of garba dancing. Most extraordinary in Gujarat â€” Navratri in Ahmedabad and Baroda is the finest garba in the world.
indianFestivals.kumbh_mela: Every 4 years in rotation between Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik, and Ujjain. The world's largest human gathering. 100 million people at Prayagraj Maha Kumbh (2025). Free. Life-altering for those with the stamina.
indianFestivals.onam: Augustâ€“September. Kerala's harvest festival. The sadya (banana leaf feast) at its most elaborate. The snake boat race at Alleppey.
indianFestivals.pushkar_camel_fair: November. The world's largest camel fair. Pushkar, Rajasthan. 50,000 camels, traders, musicians, acrobats, and tourists.
indianFestivals.hornbill_festival: December 1â€“10. Nagaland. All Naga tribes gather for cultural performances, tribal games, and traditional music. The most extraordinary cultural festival accessible in India.

visaIntelligence.foreignNationals: e-Visa available for 150+ nationalities at indianvisaonline.gov.in. Tourist e-Visa: USD 25 (30 days) or USD 80 (1 year multiple entry). Apply minimum 4 days before travel.
visaIntelligence.important: e-Visa is linked to your passport biometrically. Carry the printed e-Visa approval at all times. The 1-year multiple entry e-Visa (USD 80) is dramatically better value for anyone visiting twice in a year.
visaIntelligence.innerLinePermits: Required for Indian citizens visiting: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram. Available online at most state government portals.
visaIntelligence.restrictedAreaPermit: Required for foreign nationals in Sikkim inner areas, Andaman restricted areas, and areas near international borders. Check with tourism department of each state.

practical.electricity: Type C and D plugs. 230V 50Hz. Indian standard plug (Type D, 3 round pins) is universal throughout India.
practical.bestExchange: ATMs in major cities. Never exchange at airports â€” 8â€“12% worse rates. State Bank of India and HDFC ATMs most reliable for foreign cards.
practical.simCard: Jio or Airtel prepaid SIM â€” available at airport and any mobile shop. Requires passport copy and photo. INR 200â€“500 for 1â€“2GB daily data. Jio has best 4G coverage.
practical.water: Never drink tap water. Sealed bottled water INR 20 (1 litre) everywhere.
practical.tipping: Not mandatory but appreciated. INR 20â€“50 at restaurants. Auto-rickshaws: round up. Hotels: INR 50â€“100 for good service.
practical.apps: Ola/Uber (auto and cab), IRCTC (trains), Zomato (food delivery and restaurants), MakeMyTrip (hotels and flights), Google Maps (works excellently in India)

insiderIntelligence: India is not one destination â€” it is a continent's worth of culture, cuisine, and landscape within national borders. A person who has visited Delhi and Goa has not seen India. They have seen two very different pieces of it.

The golden rule of Indian street food: eat from the stall with the most local customers and the highest turnover. Food safety in India is about freshness and volume â€” the busy stall is always safer than the quiet one.
Indian railways is the world's most complex ticketing system. Use only the IRCTC website or app. Never buy from touts outside the station.

The most extraordinary free experiences in India: Golden Temple langar (Amritsar), sunrise at the Taj Mahal from Mehtab Bagh (across the river), morning at the Ganga ghats in Varanasi, dawn at the Living Root Bridge in Meghalaya.
Hindi is NOT spoken everywhere. In Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala, locals may not respond to Hindi and may find it presumptuous. English is the working language in South India.
Indian time (IST) is also known as 'Indian Standard Time' but informally stands for 'Indian Stretchable Time'. Meetings, events, and trains run late. Build buffer time into any schedule.
The Indian head wobble (bobbing from side to side) means 'yes', 'OK', or 'I understand'. It does NOT mean 'no'.
Most Indian temples have strict dress codes. Carry a dupatta/scarf for women and wear full-length trousers for men. Many temples do not allow leather items inside.

Bargaining is expected at markets, souvenir shops, and with auto-rickshaws where meters are not used. Start at 50% of asking price. Never bargain at restaurants or in shops with fixed prices displayed.

The best months to visit most of India are October and November â€” after the monsoon when everything is green and before the peak tourist season. October pricing is lower, crowds are thinner, and the landscape is at its most beautiful.
whyPeopleFallInLove: People arrive for the Taj Mahal. They stay when they witness something they were not expecting â€” a morning puja at a ghat they found by accident, an invitation to a family home for chai, the call to prayer and temple bells happening simultaneously from adjacent buildings. They return because India is the only country that simultaneously overwhelms you and makes you feel that you have not understood it yet, and both feelings are correct. India does not reveal itself to the person who rushes. It reveals itself to the person who accepts that they will not understand it today and comes back anyway.
localTruths: Most visitors think India is chaotic. India runs on a logic that takes three days to begin to read â€” the traffic that moves without signals, the negotiation that sounds like an argument, the hospitality that appears from nowhere. The apparent chaos is organised. The visitor who accepts this stops being frustrated and starts being amazed.

Most visitors think India is one country. India is 28 countries with one passport, one currency, and one railway system. The person who visits Delhi and Goa has visited two places that share a flag and almost nothing else. The food, language, architecture, culture, and pace are completely different. India requires more than one trip.

Most visitors think India is the ancient monuments. The ancient monuments are real and extraordinary. But the living traditions â€” the artisan weaving in Varanasi, the morning aarti at the ghats, the temple ceremony in a Bali-equivalent village in Tamil Nadu â€” are the India that cannot be found in photographs and cannot be adequately described. It requires presence.

ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.breakfast: Chandni Chowk at 7am before the shops open â€” the wholesale traders working, the temples doing morning puja, the parathas at Paranthe Wali Gali being fried in clarified butter. The oldest market street in India at its most honest hour.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.sunrise: Taj Mahal at opening, 30 minutes before sunrise â€” the most photographed building in human history, at the one hour when it belongs to almost no one. The mist on the Yamuna behind it. The marble changing colour as the sun rises. The version of this monument that exists in no travel photograph.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.neighbourhood: Varanasi ghats at 5am â€” the morning boat ride before the tour boats arrive, watching the city use the river for yoga, bathing, laundry, prayer, and cremation simultaneously. The oldest continuously inhabited city in the world being itself.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.meal: Thali at any local restaurant with locals eating â€” unlimited, regional, INR 120â€“200, every dish placed simultaneously on the banana leaf or steel plate. The meal that tells you more about where you are than any monument.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.memory: Being invited somewhere you were not expecting â€” into a home for chai, to watch a ceremony from the outer courtyard, to join a family at the ghat. India's hospitality is not a tourism product. It is a cultural practice that has existed longer than most countries.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.secret: The 5:30am on any Indian train â€” the chai vendor walking the platform, the fields appearing pale blue in the first light, your fellow passengers sharing food without being asked. The Indian railway at dawn is the most honest portrait of the country available to anyone with INR 200 and a willingness to be awake.

residentSunday: A Delhi resident with one free Sunday: 6am Lodi Garden walk before the joggers arrive â€” the 15th-century tombs in morning mist, free, extraordinary. 8am Paranthe Wali Gali in Chandni Chowk for breakfast â€” the stuffed parathas being fried in clarified butter, INR 80-120. 10am Humayun's Tomb before the tour groups â€” the prototype for the Taj Mahal with a fraction of the crowd, INR 10 for Indians. 1pm Karim's near Jama Masjid â€” the mutton burra, the seekh kebab, open since 1913. Afternoon rest. 4pm Mehrauli Archaeological Park â€” 20+ medieval monuments in a park that most Delhi residents have never visited. Free. 7pm back home. This is the Delhi that the city's residents describe when they say they love where they live.

dayMemoryTargets.arrival: The specific moment India makes itself known â€” the heat, the density, the simultaneity of ancient and modern, the smell of spices and diesel and marigolds and incense all at once. Then the first act of hospitality from a stranger: a chai offered without request, directions given with genuine investment, an invitation extended without expectation of return. The memory is the first evidence that India operates on human terms that no other country has quite matched.
dayMemoryTargets.peak: The Taj Mahal at sunrise â€” but not the standard photograph. The walk through the Great Gate at 6am when the monument appears framed by the arch, and then the 20-minute walk across the garden as the light changes on the marble. OR the Ganga Aarti in Varanasi at dusk â€” the fire, the chanting, the river, the simultaneous life and death of the same waterfront. The memory is the moment India became irreducible to any single explanation.
dayMemoryTargets.departure: The train station before departure â€” the chai wallahs, the families, the vendors, the noise, the extraordinary human density that is somehow organised. Then the specific quality of Indian light from a train window at dawn â€” the fields pale blue, the villages beginning their day, the sense of a country starting over every morning. The memory is the realisation that India is too large to have visited but exactly the right size to have experienced.

must_include: OR Golden Temple langar in Amritsar
OR one genuine local meal wherever you are
two_days.note: Two days in India should go deep in one place. The Taj Mahal deserves a full day. The Golden Temple deserves a full day. One thing done properly is infinitely better than three things rushed.

must_include: OR Rajasthan single city (Jaipur, Jodhpur, or Udaipur)
three_to_four_days.note: Three to four days in India: one region, done properly. India punishes the traveller who tries to see too much too quickly.

five_to_six_days.note: Five to six days: one circuit done properly. Now depth is possible within a region.

must_include: One full region with day trips
At least one overnight train journey
seven_plus_days.note: At 7+ days India begins to reveal itself. The overnight train is mandatory â€” not for efficiency but for experience. The train IS the India.

antiPatterns: Agra Fort AND Taj Mahal AND Fatehpur Sikri in a single day â€” each requires 2-3 hours of genuine attention. The Taj deserves its own morning. Agra Fort can follow. Fatehpur Sikri is a separate half-day.
Multiple Rajasthan cities in a single day â€” Jaipur to Jodhpur to Udaipur as a 1-day drive is a travel day disguised as a sightseeing day. Each city deserves a minimum of 2 nights.
Kerala houseboat AND Munnar hill station on the same day â€” they are 4-5 hours apart and represent completely different landscapes and experiences. Each deserves at least 2 nights.
Varanasi ghat walk AND Sarnath on the same morning â€” Varanasi ghats at dawn require 2-3 hours of unhurried presence. Sarnath (10km away) is a separate half-day.

Golden Temple in Amritsar AND Wagah Border ceremony on the same day without sufficient time â€” the Wagah ceremony is 30km from Amritsar. Attempting the Golden Temple morning AND the Wagah afternoon is physically possible but leaves neither done with full attention.
